messages:
Anna Chen: Dropped a new mock for the first-run helper strip that appears at console entry. Need quick confirmation on CTA copy, sample card order, and a11y bits before I hand off to frontend.

Sam Rivera: Looks tidy. The CTA is visually overpowering the cards right now 94 it reads like the primary action is to create, not to try a sample.

Jordan Patel: Yeah. Two copy options to consider: "Create your first project" (more decisive) vs "Start with a sample project" (more gentle). I lean to the latter for lowering friction.

Maya Singh: Accessibility check: current CTA is #2563EB on white -> contrast ~3.9:1. Fails WCAG AA for normal text. Options: darken to #1e40af (~4.6:1) or keep hue but mark as large (>=18pt bold) which we don't want. Recommend darken.

Kai Nguyen: Implementation note: darkening is trivial. Also adding a distinct focus ring is important. Proposed CSS: 

```css
button.onboard-cta:focus { outline: 3px solid #ffd54f; outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 6px }
```

Sam Rivera: Also reduce vertical padding on CTA from 16px -> 12px so it respects the vertical rhythm and doesn't visually overshadow the sample cards.

Anna Chen: On sample ordering: current is [Starter API, Search Assistant, Docs Summarizer]. I vote Starter API, Docs Summarizer, Search Assistant so the lowest-friction option sits next to the CTA.

Jordan Patel: Agreed. Search Assistant can surface infra/permissions questions early which increases drop-off.

Maya Singh: Keyboard focus order needs to be logical: CTA -> card1 -> card2 -> card3 -> dismiss control. Add aria-describedby on the CTA referencing the microcopy to help screen reader users. Also wrap the strip with role="region" and aria-label="Onboarding suggestions".

Kai Nguyen: I'll add aria-describedby="onboard-strip-desc" and the region attributes. Will also ensure the strip is reachable via skip link and that focus traps are avoided.

Sam Rivera: Microcopy suggestions (short):
- Primary CTA: "Start with a sample project"
- Helper line: "Try a prebuilt stack and see results in minutes"

Anna Chen: Love that. One more behavior question: sticky at top vs inline dismissible. Research shows sticky increases conversion but can annoy quick sessions. Idea: make it sticky for the first 3 minutes of the session, then collapse to a compact banner. That gives exposure but limits annoyance. We should A/B test.

Jordan Patel: Smart compromise. We can instrument a metric for dismiss rate and time-on-page to evaluate.

Maya Singh: For a11y, ensure the transition (sticky -> collapsed) is announced to assistive tech: use aria-live="polite" when state changes and make sure focus isn't moved unexpectedly.

Kai Nguyen: Noted. I'll prototype the behavior in a branch `onboard/strip-ephemeral` and include the aria-live announcements.

LaunchBot: Heads up 94 design freeze for first-run surfaces is tomorrow at 18:00 PT. Tagging @Kai and @Anna for final PR/assets.

Anna Chen: Plan: I'll update the Figma mock with darker CTA (#1e40af), reduced padding, reordered cards, and new copy "Start with a sample project". Uploading assets by EOD. Kai will start the accessibility-first spike. Thanks all! :slightly_smiling_face:
